## 🔬 Research Identity
::: intro-block
**Imbalance-Aware Artificial Intelligence · Urban Data Science · Reproducible Analytical Systems**

Jesús Cáceres-Tello is a PhD in Statistical Studies specialising in methodological artificial intelligence and urban data science. He combines academic research with extensive experience in public sector digital systems and applied data science.

His work focuses on the evaluation of predictive models under real-world constraints, with emphasis on:

- Urban environmental modelling and air quality forecasting  
- Machine learning under class imbalance  
- Time series forecasting and temporal validation  
- Hybrid and deep learning architectures  
- Performance–cost trade-off analysis  
- Reproducible research and open science frameworks  
- AI-supported STEM education  

His research contributes to the development of transparent, reproducible, and operational AI systems for sustainable urban environments.
:::

## 🎯 Research Mission
::: intro-block
The objective of his research is to develop methodologically coherent AI frameworks for urban sustainability and STEM education.

This includes:

- Evaluating models under structural imbalance  
- Designing reproducible analytical pipelines  
- Integrating computational efficiency into model comparison  
- Supporting data-driven decision-making in institutional contexts  

His research is developed within a broader programme in applied data science for sustainable systems.
:::

## 🏗 Research Infrastructure & Open Science
::: intro-block
All research is developed following open science and reproducibility principles.

All research projects are developed within a structured computational framework:

- Git-based version control  
- Public repositories with DOI integration (Zenodo)  
- Reproducible scripts and notebooks (R, Python, Quarto)  
- Time-based validation strategies  
- Transparent and standardised performance reporting  

Each publication is supported by:

- An open repository  
- Executable code  
- Structured documentation  
- Publicly accessible data sources  

This approach ensures traceability, transparency, and methodological consistency across all research outputs.
:::
